_fuente: Cambridge English, Pre A1 Starters / A1 Movers / A2 Flyers Handbook for teachers 2024, «Grammar and Structures List»: Starters pp. 29-30, Movers pp. 52-53 (lo nuevo en A1), Flyers p. 77 (lo nuevo en A2). Cada nivel exige además todo lo de los niveles anteriores.

starters.name: Nouns: singular and plural (incl. irregular), countable and uncountable, names
starters.eg: Would you like an orange? Lemons are yellow. Pat has six mice. I eat rice for lunch.

starters.name: Adjectives, including possessive adjectives
starters.eg: He's a small boy. His name is Yusef.

starters.name: Determiners (a/an, the, some, this/these)
starters.eg: It's a banana. This is an apple. I want some milk. These books are blue.

starters.name: Pronouns: demonstrative, personal, possessive, interrogative and 'one'
starters.eg: This is my car. Can you see me? Which is Anna? I'd like one. This is mine!

starters.name: Present simple (positive, negative, question, imperative, short answers, contractions)
starters.eg: Nick is happy. I don't like eggs. Eat your lunch! Is that your sister? Yes, it is.

starters.name: Present continuous (not with future reference)
starters.eg: What are you doing? The cat's sleeping.

starters.name: Can for ability
starters.eg: The baby can wave.

starters.name: Can for requests and permission
starters.eg: Can I have some birthday cake?

starters.name: Have (got) for possession
starters.eg: Have you got a pen? She hasn't got a dog.

starters.name: Adverbs (now, here, too)
starters.eg: I'm colouring it now. My grandma lives here. She lives here too.

starters.name: Conjunctions (and)
starters.eg: I've got a pen and a pencil.

starters.name: Prepositions of place and time
starters.eg: Put the clock next to the picture. We go to school in the morning.

starters.name: Question words (who, where…)
starters.eg: Who is that man? Where is Alex?

starters.name: Impersonal you
starters.eg: How do you spell that?

starters.name: Have + object + infinitive
starters.eg: Lucy has a book to read.

starters.name: -ing forms as nouns
starters.eg: Swimming is good.

starters.name: Let's
starters.eg: Let's go to the zoo!

starters.name: Like + v + ing
starters.eg: I like swimming.

starters.name: There is / There are
starters.eg: There is a monkey in the tree. There are some books on the table.

starters.name: Would like + noun or verb
starters.eg: I would like some grapes. Would you like to colour that ball?

starters.name: Happy birthday!
starters.eg: You're eight today! Happy Birthday!

starters.name: Here you are
starters.eg: Would you like an apple? Yes, please. Here you are.

starters.name: Me too!
starters.eg: I like football. Me too.

starters.name: So do I
starters.eg: I love hippos. So do I.

starters.name: Story about + ing
starters.eg: This is a story about playing football.

starters.name: What (a/an) + adjective + noun
starters.eg: What a good dog! What beautiful fish!

starters.name: What now?
starters.eg: OK! The egg is in the box. What now?

movers.name: Indirect objects
movers.eg: Give it to the teacher!

movers.name: Comparative and superlative adjectives
movers.eg: Your house is bigger than mine. Anna is my best friend.

movers.name: Past simple, regular and irregular forms
movers.eg: We went to the park yesterday. Did you go to the cinema? Yes, I did.

movers.name: Verb + infinitive
movers.eg: I want to go home. He started to laugh.

movers.name: Verb + -ing
movers.eg: I went riding on Saturday.

movers.name: Infinitive of purpose
movers.eg: She went to town to buy a toothbrush.

movers.name: Want / ask someone to do something
movers.eg: He wants the teacher to tell a story.

movers.name: Must for obligation
movers.eg: He must do his homework. You mustn't give the rabbit cheese.

movers.name: Have (got) to / had to
movers.eg: I've got to go. He had to draw a whale for homework.

movers.name: Shall for offers
movers.eg: Shall I help you wash the car, Mum?

movers.name: Could (past form of can)
movers.eg: I could see some birds in the tree.

movers.name: Adverbs (never, loudly, a lot)
movers.eg: She never eats meat. He sang loudly. My mother talks a lot.

movers.name: Comparative and superlative adverbs
movers.eg: My brother reads more quickly than my sister. I like ice cream best.

movers.name: Conjunctions (because)
movers.eg: I went home because I was tired.

movers.name: Prepositions of time (after, on)
movers.eg: She plays with her friends after school. He plays badminton on Saturdays.

movers.name: Question words (why, when)
movers.eg: Why is he talking to her? When does school start?

movers.name: Relative clauses (who, which, where)
movers.eg: Vicky is the girl who is riding a bike. That is the DVD which my friend gave me.

movers.name: What is / was the weather like?
movers.eg: What was the weather like last weekend?

movers.name: What's the matter?
movers.eg: What's the matter, Daisy? Have you got a stomach-ache?

movers.name: How / What about + noun or -ing
movers.eg: How about going to the cinema on Wednesday afternoon?

movers.name: When clauses (not with future meaning)
movers.eg: When he got home, he had his dinner.

movers.name: Go for a + noun
movers.eg: Yesterday we went for a drive in my brother's new car.

movers.name: Be called + noun
movers.eg: A baby cat is called a kitten.

movers.name: Be good at + noun
movers.eg: She's very good at basketball.

movers.name: I think / I know …
movers.eg: I think he's very nice.

flyers.name: Past continuous (interrupted actions and background)
flyers.eg: I was walking down the road when I saw her. It was a very cold day and snow was falling.

flyers.name: Present perfect
flyers.eg: Have you ever been to the circus? He's just eaten his dinner.

flyers.name: Be going to
flyers.eg: It isn't going to rain today.

flyers.name: Will
flyers.eg: Will you do your homework this evening? I won't buy her a CD.

flyers.name: Might
flyers.eg: Vicky might come to the party.

flyers.name: May
flyers.eg: The bus may not come today because there is a lot of snow.

flyers.name: Shall for suggestions
flyers.eg: Shall we have a picnic in the park?

flyers.name: Could
flyers.eg: You could invite Robert to the football game.

flyers.name: Should
flyers.eg: Should we take a towel to the swimming pool?

flyers.name: Tag questions
flyers.eg: That's John's book, isn't it?

flyers.name: Adverbs (yet)
flyers.eg: I haven't bought my brother's birthday present yet.

flyers.name: Conjunctions (so)
flyers.eg: I didn't want to walk home so I went on the bus.

flyers.name: If clauses (zero conditional)
flyers.eg: If it's sunny, we go swimming.

flyers.name: Where clauses
flyers.eg: My grandmother has forgotten where she put her glasses.

flyers.name: Before / after clauses (not with future reference)
flyers.eg: I finished my homework before I played football.

flyers.name: Be / look / sound / feel / taste / smell like
flyers.eg: What's your new teacher like? That sounds like the baby upstairs.

flyers.name: Make somebody / something + adjective
flyers.eg: That smell makes me hungry!

flyers.name: What time …?
flyers.eg: What time does the film start?

flyers.name: What else / What next?
flyers.eg: What else shall I draw?

flyers.name: See you soon / later / tomorrow
flyers.eg: See you next week, Mrs Ball!

flyers.name: Be made of
flyers.eg: The toy is made of wood.
